title: A local lint run with no base cannot read as a pass
why: Incident, Oct 28 (orchestrator): batch 5's local `ci-job gates --lint` passed, then CI's gates job failed on lint/check_comment_narration.py (dated comments from c148), costing a CI run.
note: Debt. Measured by triage 10 on main 4e913588: with --base origin/main the lint plan runs the comment narration check; with no --base it skips it, and the run still reads as a pass. The silent-undo and STE lint steps skip the same way. Next cloud lane: bin/ci-job --lint with no --base exits non-zero and names each skipped pull-request step, or takes origin/main as the default base; the lane picks one and says why in the decision that holds ci-job. Red first: today's no-base run over a planted dated comment passes. Touches bin/ci-job and its tests only. Needs no answer. Port: no; ci-job lives in claude-settings. Placed ahead of c166 (triage 10, Oct 28): every lane and batch runs this check, and a false pass costs a 50 to 60 min CI run. Done: merged in batch 6 (PR #760, main 599dd58b, Oct 28 05:45 CDT). Pick: no --base defaults to origin/main, as CI does; if that does not resolve, it prints one unknown line naming the skipped pull-request steps and exits 2. Notes: a plain `ci-job gates` with no base still skips those steps and can exit 0 (lanes run only --lint); the brief template's extra ste-changed run is c173.
